tennessee_state_programs.title: Tennessee HOPE Scholarship
tennessee_state_programs.description: The Tennessee HOPE Scholarship provides up to $6,000 per year for students at four-year institutions and $3,000 per year at two-year institutions. Based on academic merit, not financial need. Funds are applied to tuition and mandatory fees first; any amount exceeding direct costs may be refunded to the student for use toward living expenses including rent, food, and utilities. Students must have a 21 ACT or 3.0 GPA and be a Tennessee resident.
eligibility_bullets: Must be a Tennessee resident
Must have a minimum 21 ACT composite or 3.0 GPA
Must enroll at an eligible Tennessee postsecondary institution
Must be a first-time freshman or continuing student meeting renewal criteria
Funds exceeding tuition and fees may be refunded for living expenses

tennessee_state_programs.title: Tennessee HOPE Access Grant
tennessee_state_programs.description: The HOPE Access Grant provides up to $2,750 per year at four-year institutions for Tennessee residents who have between an 18-20 ACT score or 2.75-2.99 GPA. This grant supplements tuition costs and any excess after tuition may be refunded to students for living expenses.
eligibility_bullets: Must be a Tennessee resident
Must have 18-20 ACT composite or 2.75-2.99 GPA
Must enroll at an eligible Tennessee institution
Available for first two semesters only

tennessee_state_programs.title: Tennessee Promise - Last Dollar Scholarship
tennessee_state_programs.description: Tennessee Promise is a last-dollar scholarship covering tuition and mandatory fees at community and technical colleges for recent Tennessee high school graduates. After Pell Grants and HOPE are applied, Tennessee Promise covers remaining tuition. This stacking approach maximizes refund potential from need-based grants.
eligibility_bullets: Must be a Tennessee high school graduate
Must complete FAFSA and Tennessee Promise application
Must complete community service hours
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress
Covers tuition and fees not covered by Pell or HOPE

tennessee_state_programs.title: Tennessee Student Assistance Award (TSAA)
tennessee_state_programs.description: Need-based grant for Tennessee residents attending eligible in-state institutions. Awards up to $4,000 per year based on financial need determined by FAFSA. Funds applied to institutional charges; when combined with other aid exceeding direct costs, may produce a refund usable for off-campus living expenses.
eligibility_bullets: Must be a Tennessee resident
Must demonstrate financial need via FAFSA
Must attend an eligible Tennessee institution
Award amount varies by need and available funding

faith_based_scholarships.title: United Methodist Higher Education Foundation General Scholarship
faith_based_scholarships.description: Merit and need-based scholarships for United Methodist students attending one of the 100+ United Methodist-related colleges and universities. Awards range from $500 to $5,000. Funds disbursed directly to student accounts; amounts exceeding tuition are refunded for living expenses.
eligibility_bullets: Must be an active member of the United Methodist Church
Must attend a United Methodist-related institution
Must maintain at least a 2.5 GPA
Both merit and need-based criteria considered

faith_based_scholarships.title: Presbyterian Church (USA) Student Opportunity Scholarship
faith_based_scholarships.description: Financial assistance for Presbyterian students attending Presbyterian-related colleges or other accredited institutions. Awards up to $3,000 based on financial need and church involvement. Scholarship funds may be used for tuition, room, board, and other educational expenses.
eligibility_bullets: Must be an active member of the Presbyterian Church (USA)
Must demonstrate financial need
Must be enrolled as an undergraduate student
Church involvement verification required

faith_based_scholarships.title: Scholarships for Lutheran Students
faith_based_scholarships.description: ELCA Fund for Leaders provides scholarships to Lutheran students preparing for ministry or enrolled at ELCA-affiliated colleges. Awards up to $5,000 per year for undergraduate students. Funds can be applied to any educational cost including off-campus living.
eligibility_bullets: Must be an active member of an ELCA congregation
Must be enrolled or planning to enroll at an accredited institution
Both ministry-track and general scholarships available
Financial need and academic merit considered

talent_based_scholarships.title: National YoungArts Foundation Award
talent_based_scholarships.description: Awards for talented young artists ages 15-18 or in grades 10-12 in visual, literary, design, and performing arts including music. Cash awards from $250 to $10,000 based on artistic merit. Music applicants may audition on any instrument including flute, piano, violin, voice, and more. Awards disbursed directly to students.
eligibility_bullets: Must be 15-18 years old or in grades 10-12
Must be a US citizen or permanent resident
Applicants submit work in one of 10 artistic disciplines
Music applicants may audition on any orchestral instrument, piano, voice, or composition

talent_based_scholarships.title: Mu Phi Epsilon Music Scholarship
talent_based_scholarships.sponsor: Mu Phi Epsilon International Music Fraternity
talent_based_scholarships.description: Scholarships for music students who demonstrate outstanding musical ability. Awards range from $1,000 to $5,000 for undergraduate and graduate students. Open to all instrumentalists, vocalists, and composers. Flutists, pianists, and other instrumentalists are encouraged to apply. Funds disbursed to student for educational and living expenses.
eligibility_bullets: Must be enrolled in a music program at an accredited institution
Must demonstrate outstanding musical ability
Open to all instrument types and vocalists
Membership in Mu Phi Epsilon not required

talent_based_scholarships.title: Flute Society of Greater Washington Young Artist Competition
talent_based_scholarships.description: Annual competition scholarship for young flutists providing cash awards of $500-$2,500. Open to flutists ages 16-27. Awards can be used for any educational purpose including tuition, lessons, living expenses, and instrument purchases.
eligibility_bullets: Must be a flutist ages 16-27
Open to US and international students
Audition-based selection process
Awards may be used for any educational purpose

talent_based_scholarships.title: National Federation of Music Clubs Music Scholarships
talent_based_scholarships.description: Multiple scholarship programs for young musicians including instrumental, vocal, and composition categories. Awards from $500 to $10,000. Available to student musicians at all levels who demonstrate musical talent. All instrument types including flute, brass, strings, and keyboard are eligible.
eligibility_bullets: Must be a US citizen
Must demonstrate musical talent through audition or application
Multiple competition categories at state and national levels
Both junior and senior divisions available

housing_support_programs.title: Federal Pell Grant
housing_support_programs.description: Need-based federal grant providing up to $7,395 per year for undergraduate students. When combined with institutional scholarships and other aid that exceed the cost of tuition and fees, the excess is refunded to the student and can be used for off-campus housing, food, transportation, and other living expenses. Pell Grants are the foundation of many students' financial aid packages.
eligibility_bullets: Must demonstrate financial need via FAFSA
Must be an undergraduate student
Must be enrolled at an eligible institution
Cannot have a bachelor's degree already
Excess funds after tuition are refunded for living expenses

housing_support_programs.title: Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant (FSEOG)
housing_support_programs.description: Campus-based need grant for undergraduates with exceptional financial need. Awards from $100 to $4,000 per year. Priority given to Pell Grant recipients. Funds applied to educational costs; when combined with other aid exceeding direct costs, produces refund for off-campus living expenses.
eligibility_bullets: Must demonstrate exceptional financial need
Must be an undergraduate student
Priority given to Pell Grant recipients
Award depends on institutional funding availability

coa_adjustment_resources.title: Cost of Attendance Appeal Process (Professional Judgment)
coa_adjustment_resources.sponsor: U.S. Department of Education / Individual Institutions
coa_adjustment_resources.description: Federal regulations allow financial aid administrators to use Professional Judgment to adjust a student's Cost of Attendance (COA) to reflect actual living expenses. Students living off-campus can request a COA increase to include actual rent, utilities, and food costs. A higher COA means more financial aid eligibility, potentially producing larger refunds that can be used for housing.
eligibility_bullets: Available to all students receiving federal financial aid
Must document actual off-campus living expenses
Requires contacting your school's financial aid office
Schools have discretion in adjusting COA
Can result in additional grant or loan eligibility
